prompt:
Check one candidate model relation against sentences of a long engineering document. Unit ids show the order of the sentences in the document; the sentences come from different places.

Candidate: Capacity Assessment Module provides "Airport Acceptance Rate" to Slot Allocation Engine (an information or material flow).

Evidence sentences used to propose the candidate:
S225: The Slot Allocation Engine proposes regulated departure and arrival opportunities by matching demand from the Demand Prediction Service to constraints supplied by the Capacity Assessment Module.
S226: The primary inputs are the Flight Intent Message, the Airport Capacity Plan, the current Airport Acceptance Rate, runway metering limits, and airspace sector loading conditions.
S340: Late airspace capacity changes are treated as high-priority operational updates because they can invalidate demand forecasts, slot allocations, and airport acceptance assumptions already in use.
S341: When a late reduction occurs, the Capacity Assessment Module recalculates the effective Airport Acceptance Rate and passes the revised assumption into the operational planning cycle.

Other sentences of the same document that mention this item, a similarly named item, or another element that produces or sends such an item:
S005: Seasonal thunderstorms, coastal fog, strong crosswinds, and convective reroutes frequently reduce the effective Airport Acceptance Rate across the network.
S046: The shared operational picture includes Flight Intent Message status, Airport Capacity Plan assumptions, Target Off Block Time values, Calculated Takeoff Time values, Airport Acceptance Rate constraints, Common Situation Display content, Tactical Regulation Proposal status, Collaborative Decision Log entries, and Post Operations Report outputs.
S066: The Capacity Assessment Module combines the runway declaration, weather outlook, airspace constraints, stand readiness, and ground resource assumptions into a proposed Airport Acceptance Rate by period.
S067: The proposed Airport Acceptance Rate is tested against the demand profile to identify overloads, underused capacity, and points where a Ground Delay Program may become necessary.
S107: The Capacity Assessment Module combines demand projections with the Airport Capacity Plan to determine whether a published Airport Acceptance Rate remains feasible.
S132: The Capacity Assessment Module compares that demand with the Airport Capacity Plan and the current Airport Acceptance Rate before recommending operating limits.
S155: The arrival workspace shows expected landing demand, stand allocation risk, inbound regulation effects, and handling readiness indicators needed to protect the Airport Acceptance Rate.
S190: The Airport Duty Manager verifies that airfield operations checks have been completed before requesting changes to Airport Acceptance Rate values or departure metering assumptions.
S252: The Capacity Assessment Module applies the active Airport Capacity Plan and Airport Acceptance Rate to determine whether the proposed demand pattern remains operationally feasible.
S286: The Regional Flow Manager is notified when local resequencing threatens to erode the planned departure rate in the Airport Capacity Plan.
S309: Shortages are often localized by apron sector, so the same nominal fleet of equipment can support one stand cluster while leaving another cluster unable to dispatch departures at the planned rate.
S351: The Capacity Assessment Module compares that demand with the active Airport Acceptance Rate, runway configuration, taxiway constraints, and sector limits.
S358: The Tower Supervisor monitors whether the planned release rate remains compatible with departure spacing and runway crossing demand.
S383: The Ground Handling Dispatcher updates remaining fluid inventory and truck serviceability when replenishment, contamination, or equipment faults affect the planned treatment rate.
S395: Arrival regulation begins when the Demand Prediction Service shows that inbound demand will exceed the Airport Acceptance Rate within the planning horizon.
S400: The Capacity Assessment Module calculates candidate Airport Acceptance Rate values for each runway configuration and exposes the operational basis for each value on the Common Situation Display.
S401: The Tower Supervisor confirms whether the proposed landing rate is compatible with runway occupancy, missed approach protection, and local spacing constraints.
S412: Diversion triggers are monitored continuously and include predicted holding beyond operator fuel thresholds, loss of required approach capability, sustained sector saturation, and runway availability below the minimum safe acceptance rate.
S417: All rate changes, rejected options, coordination outcomes, and effective times are written to the Audit Event Ledger for later review.
S424: Arrival demand is monitored against the Airport Acceptance Rate, current sequencing performance, and any Ground Delay Program that remains in effect.
S454: North Runway Meter reduces the departure release rate when surface surveillance shows that runway-entry queues are approaching the metering threshold.
S493: The Demand Prediction Service compares amended Flight Intent Message data with the Airport Capacity Plan and the current Airport Acceptance Rate to show whether a diversion can be absorbed without creating unsafe demand peaks.
S535: Nightjar shall suppress handler-exception annotations for arriving flights unless the exception changes the Airport Acceptance Rate or a regulated arrival sequence.
S595: For departure-dominated overload, the conversion result is normally an airport departure rate, a constrained departure fix allocation, or a proposed spacing value at the runway release point.
S596: For arrival-dominated overload, the result is expressed as an adjusted Airport Acceptance Rate or a metered arrival stream for Arrival Regulation Console.
S669: The Slot Allocation Engine evaluates the candidate swap against active Ground Delay Program constraints, Calculated Takeoff Time integrity, Target Off Block Time dependencies, and Airport Acceptance Rate commitments.
S696: The Regional Flow Manager reviews the published constraint when it changes the usable runway rate, taxi-out predictability, or the feasibility of the active demand plan.
S698: If the event reduces arrival throughput, the Arrival Regulation Console applies the revised Airport Acceptance Rate after confirmation by the Regional Flow Manager.
S757: The Arrival Regulation Console may show inbound connection pressure as context for arrival rate discussions, but it does not convert passenger handling needs into a separate arrival priority scheme.
S774: Operational segregation shall prevent a single user from creating, approving, and technically concealing a material change to a Ground Delay Program, Airport Acceptance Rate, or Tactical Regulation Proposal.
S803: Capacity changes made through the Capacity Assessment Module shall be correlated with the active Airport Capacity Plan and Airport Acceptance Rate used at the time of allocation.
S816: The Airport Duty Manager shall own airport capacity declarations, including Airport Capacity Plan records and Airport Acceptance Rate values.
S853: The Capacity Assessment Module shall record the available Airport Acceptance Rate used in each baseline so that avoided cancellation estimates remain traceable.
S953: The system should not automatically impose a Ground Delay Program, change an Airport Acceptance Rate, or alter a tactical measure without authorized human confirmation.
S977: Ground Delay Program decisions, Tactical Regulation Proposal review, and Airport Acceptance Rate changes should be visible to affected participants before they are applied whenever operational time permits.

Answer "supported" only if the document states that Capacity Assessment Module produces or sends this item AND that Slot Allocation Engine receives or uses the same item (it may be named more briefly in one sentence), and no other sentence shows that the item Slot Allocation Engine uses comes from a different producer or is a different item with a similar name. Answer "unsupported" if the sentences describe different items, the wrong elements, the opposite direction, or if another producer of the item the consumer uses is stated. Answer "uncertain" if the text is not clear enough. Return JSON {"verdict": ..., "reason": "one sentence"}.
response: {"verdict":"supported","reason":"S225 says the Slot Allocation Engine uses constraints supplied by the Capacity Assessment Module, and S226 lists the current Airport Acceptance Rate among its inputs. S66, S341 and S400 show the module calculates and proposes the rate. No sentence names a different producer of the rate the engine uses; the Airport Duty Manager owns declarations (S816) and the Arrival Regulation Console applies the rate (S698), but neither is shown supplying it to the engine."}
